content.comment_body: Hello, I've encountered an issue. About a year ago, I deployed my web application using [product_name] [version_no], and everything worked flawlessly with fast loading on both mobile and desktop browsers. In January 2024, I received a notification from AWS Elastic Beanstalk that my environment version would be terminated due to an updated version policy. So, I upgraded to the latest [product_name] [version_no] and redeployed on AWS. Unfortunately, my web app now loads slowly on first access, the connection is sometimes flagged as insecure, and there are occasional lags within the app. I tried upgrading the instance type from t2.micro to t3.large. While the app runs more smoothly overall, the initial load is still slow and there are occasional connection timeouts in the browser. Has anyone else experienced these issues and found a solution?

analysis.insight_summary: The user reports that after upgrading from [product_name] [version_no] to [product_name] [version_no] for deploying a web app on AWS Elastic Beanstalk, there was a notable drop in performance, including slower first-page loads, lag within the app, and periodic connection errors. Prior to the upgrade, the app worked seamlessly on both mobile and PC. The problems persist even after switching to a higher instance type, pointing to a software compatibility or version issue rather than hardware limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that newer software releases should offer the same or better performance and security as earlier versions, regardless of infrastructure modifications, providing a consistently fast and reliable browsing experience.
